newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Diatide seeks cancer drug pact.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Diatide seeks cancer drug pact.

text.p: Diatide Inc is in talks with potential partners for developing its cancer pain drug, the company's chief executive Richard Dean said on Friday.
Dean said Diatide was in partnership talks with several large pharmaceutical companies with "well-recognized names" in the oncology field.
"We want a partner to provide funding (for clinical trials) and help us market the product," Dean said in an interview.

Diatide's main business is developing agents for nuclear medical diagnostic imaging but last year licensed the drug, a compound containing a radioisotope and a binding agent, from the Department of Energy's Brookhaven National Laboratory.
The drug's aim is to treat cancer-related bone pain.
Diatide expects to start a Phase III clinical trial with the drug upon signing a partnership deal. "We're looking for the early part of next year for that to happen," Dean said.
Last year Diatide signed a partnership pact with Norway's Hafslund Nycomed A/S to develop Diatide's peptide-based imaging agents.
Londonderry, N.H.-based Diatide expects to file for U.S. Food and Drug administration approval for the first its imaging agents by mid-1997, Dean said.

The company then aims to file for two of the agents with the FDA a year, he said. The first filing will be an agent for detecting deep vein thrombosis, or clotting, followed by others for tumors including melanomas and lung cancers.
The agents use a peptide to deliver technetium to disease targets. The technetium emits a gamma ray that is picked up by gamma camera.
Diatide went public in June at 8-1/2. Its stock shed 1/2 at 6-7/8 Friday.
The company faces competition from major players including a DuPont Co -Merck and Co Inc joint venture, Schering AG and Mallinckrodt Inc.

But Dean said Diatide has a two-year lead on its nearest challenger, DuPont-Merck, in peptide-based imaging agents. He said the Diatide has also filed for patents that, if granted, could stymie DuPont-Merck's efforts.
The deal with Nycomed included a $10 million capital investment and $10 million for five years of research and development.
Dean said Diatide will also receive "substantial" milestone payments when the imaging agents are filed with the FDA and when they are approved. He declined to detail the amounts.
As of June 30 the company had $21 million in cash, he said.
In company could see its first sales in late 1998 or in 1999, reaching profitability 18 months after that, Dean said.
It posted a net loss of $6.4 million in 1995, or a pro forma loss of $0.90 a share.
